what_happened.line: The commission said it will consult legal counsel and the state about a possible new vote on the Pratt Street and Lake View sewer extension, and report back quickly.
Residents questioned the total cost of the extension, grinder pumps, connection fees, betterments and loan terms, and some said costs had not been disclosed to them.
The engineer presented the Pratt Street and Lake View extension, including that homeowners pay private costs for the grinder pump and its installation.
The Arbor Street group was told to establish need through the engineers' review of the CWMP before any change to the sewer service area.
The board voted to send grease trap non-compliance notices under the regulation; the vote record was not audible in the captions.

why_it_matters: Homeowners on Pratt Street and Lake View may face up-front connection, inflow and capacity fees, private grinder pump costs and betterment charges on top of sewer rates, so the cost questions raised here bear directly on their bills.
Whether a new vote is held depends on the advice of counsel and the state, and that advice decides if affected residents get another say on the extension.
Businesses with grease traps face daily fines if they stay out of compliance after notice.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission heard that the two lowest bids for the SRF sewer expansion came in under projections; the engineers are reviewing them.
A bid recommendation is expected at the May 12 meeting, and a resident informational meeting is planned for the May 26 televised meeting.
The commission discussed how grease trap rules apply at One Main Street, and noted that grease damages pumps and that replacing a pump station is very costly.
The chair said the three Town Meeting sewer articles have no financial impact on the town, and suggested the next board consider whether all ten pump stations need SCADA.
Two members left the board at this meeting; the only motion was adjournment, and no votes were recorded.

why_it_matters: Sewer expansion bids that come in under projections bear on what the project costs the users and the town, and residents are due an informational meeting before the project goes further.
Grease trap enforcement and pump station upkeep are costs the sewer system carries, and the question of SCADA on all ten pump stations is left to the next board.

votes.motion: Move forward with Wright Pierce on the grant application for manhole inspection, committing the up-front amount, with obligation limited to the match if the grant is awarded.
Go into executive session under MGL c.38 s.21A(3) to discuss litigation strategy (Hollis Hills LLC v. Lunenburg ZBA), not to return to open session.
votes.outcome: roll call taken; ayes heard from each member, result implied but not stated

budget_items.what_was_said: A vendor proposed inspecting over 300 manholes; members thought the price was high and it was not in this or next year's budget.
A grant of up to a set amount could fund the study, with a small up-front cost and a 25 percent match if awarded; the engineer would share some risk.

budget_items.topic: Funding the match from engineering line
budget_items.what_was_said: Members thought the match could be covered this year from unspent engineering funds.
Expenses rise modestly while revenue is projected to rise more, giving a positive operating result with no retained earnings transfer.

budget_items.topic: Betterment fund cash flow and enterprise fund
budget_items.what_was_said: The betterment fund is running negative cash flow this year, making the overall enterprise fund show a deficit, though projections to 2028 stay secure.
A warrant article would create a stabilization fund to hold capacity fees collected for capacity bought from Fitchburg.
A warrant article for the Pleasant View sewer, serving a dozen users, with possible low-interest state revolving fund financing.
An insurance product for private sewer laterals was described with an approximate annual cost.

budget_items.topic: Flow meter repair and Fitchburg billing
budget_items.what_was_said: The meter rebuilt after an accident has lasted about half its expected life; Fitchburg is paid based on its readings.

budget_items.topic: Betterment and connection fee for extension
budget_items.what_was_said: Connecting before the town accepts a privately funded line costs half the prior betterment fee; later connections pay the full fee.
A member recalled the cost of an external grease trap installation.
A member told of a state fine in another town; regulation provides a per-violation penalty.
The pump station wet well cleaning cost was recalled as a few thousand dollars for all stations.

decisions.decision: Notice of non-compliance to be revised to cover both grease traps and interceptors, with a checkbox for each, on one form.
Once the form is ready, the office will begin sending notices and assessing fees to non-compliant establishments.
Seek a joint meeting with the Board of Health about grease trap inspections, no later than June.
Proposal to change monthly reporting to quarterly requires a regulation change, to be put on a future agenda.
Notices on grease violations should go to landlords as well as tenants; town counsel to be consulted on landlord liability.
Business manager to schedule the sewer insurance company at a future televised meeting.
Members to give written feedback on the privately funded extension policy draft before the next meeting.
Annual report approval deferred to the April 14 meeting.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted unanimously to move forward with its engineer on a state grant application for a manhole inspection study, with its obligation limited to the match if awarded.
The commission agreed to begin sending grease trap non-compliance notices and assessing fees once a revised form covering both traps and interceptors is ready.
Members asked that grease violation notices go to landlords as well as tenants, and that town counsel be consulted on landlord liability.
The commission will seek a joint meeting with the Board of Health on grease trap inspections, no later than June.
Approval of the annual report was deferred to the April 14 meeting, and the commission closed by going into executive session on litigation.

why_it_matters: Restaurants and their landlords may begin receiving grease trap notices and fees, and responsibility for shared interceptors is still being settled.
A grant could pay for a manhole inspection study the sewer budget does not currently cover, with the match expected to come from unspent engineering funds this year.
watch_next: The April 14 meeting, where approval of the annual report is expected.
Written member feedback on the privately funded extension policy draft, due before the next meeting.
